name: Sishtagurunatheswarar Temple, Thiruthuraiyur
deity: Shiva as Sishtagurunatheswarar (Pasupatheeswarar), with the Goddesses Sivaloka Nayaki and Poongothai Nayaki
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam of Nadu Nadu near the Then Pennai, sung by Sundarar (8th century)
summary: North of Panruti, by the Then Pennai, the Lord of Thiruthuraiyur is remembered as the aged ferryman who carried Sundarar across the flooded river — and as the guru who taught him the path of penance.

sections.history: Thiruthuraiyur is a village of Panruti taluk in Cuddalore district, about 9 km north of Panruti, in the country watered by the Then Pennai. Its Shiva temple is one of the 276 Paadal Petra Sthalams and one of the shrines of Nadu Nadu. Sundarar came here from Thiruvennainallur, a short way upstream, and sang a pathigam that praises both the Lord of Thiruthuraiyur and the holiness of the Pennai itself. The village is also remembered in the Shaiva Siddhanta tradition as linked to Arulnandi Sivachariyar, the foremost disciple of Meykandar, and a memorial to him stands in the neighbourhood.
sections.architecture: This is a modest Dravidian village temple with the Lord enshrined as a lingam in the sanctum. The Goddess is worshipped in two forms, as Sivaloka Nayaki and as Poongothai Nayaki, the one adorned with flower garlands. The temple's sacred water is the Surya Pushkarini, and the river Pennai, which the Lord himself is said to have crossed, flows close by.
sections.legends: Tradition tells that when Sundarar set out from Thiruvennainallur, the Then Pennai was in flood and he could not cross to reach this shrine. He prayed and sang, and an elderly couple appeared and offered to ferry him over; on the far bank they revealed themselves as Shiva and Parvati, seated upon the bull. Here, it is said, Sundarar asked the Lord for the path of penance, and the Lord instructed him — and so he is worshipped as Sishtagurunathar, the Lord who became the teacher.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri, Karthigai Deepam, Arudra Darshanam and the monthly pradosham are the customary observances, and Sundarar's day in the month of Aadi is remembered at a shrine so closely tied to his story; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thiruthuraiyur is a quiet village temple, best visited as one stage of a short pilgrimage along the Pennai: Thiruvennainallur, where Sundarar was claimed by the Lord, and Thiruthuraiyur, where the Lord carried him across the river and taught him. Students of Shaiva Siddhanta also come to honour the memory of Arulnandi Sivachariyar.

visit.timings: Open in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals and the festival bronzes.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruthuraiyur lies about 9 km north of Panruti by way of Pudupettai and Chinnapettai, with regular buses from Panruti; Villupuram is about 16 km away. Villupuram is the nearest major railway junction and Panruti has its own station; Chennai and Tiruchirappalli are the nearest major airports, with Puducherry also within reach by road.
